signals.title: Agent in a Bottle: Can LLM Agents Turn Their Capabilities Into Cheap, Scalable Artifacts?
signals.content: Large language models (LLMs) can solve many narrow tasks, but querying them separately for millions of related instances can be prohibitively expensive. Can LLM agents autonomously create cheaper solutions for such workloads? We call this ability "bottling": the ability to turn general capabilities into task-specific solutions that balance answer quality and amortised cost. We introduce BOTTLED, a benchmark in which agents receive an entire unlabelled workload and must complete it under fixed time, compute and LLM API budgets. Agents choose their own approach, such as training a small model or writing a reusable program. Across ten models and three tasks, we find that strong zero-shot task performance does not reliably translate into strong bottling capabilities. Models with similar zero-shot scores can differ substantially after bottling, and 48 of 60 bottling runs score below the lower bound of the 95% confidence interval of their model's zero-shot performance. Moreover, 31 of 60 runs underperform the stronger of two small-model distillation baselines with the same token budget. Nevertheless, bottling can yield substantial savings: on query-product relevance classification, Opus 5 retains about 82% of its zero-shot macro-F1 at roughly 657 times lower reported cost. Bottling is also competitive with Jev, a "system one" model built especially for cheap, repetitive inference: Opus 5 on the same task recovers about 94% of Jev's macro-F1 at a quarter of Jev's projected full-workload cost. BOTTLED provides a basis for evaluating and improving agents' ability to invest limited resources in reusable solutions for large, repetitive workloads.

signals.brief_en:
Title: Agent in a Bottle – Can LLM agents turn their general abilities into cheap, scalable artifacts?

Large language models excel at many narrow tasks, yet running them millions of times is often cost‑prohibitive. The proposed "bottling" concept asks whether an LLM agent can autonomously create a task‑specific solution that balances answer quality with amortised cost. The BOTTLED benchmark gives agents an unlabelled workload and fixed limits on time, compute, and API usage; agents may train a small model, write reusable code, or adopt other strategies.

Key findings (10 models, 3 tasks):
- Strong zero‑shot performance does not guarantee bottling success; many runs fall below the 95% confidence lower bound of their own zero‑shot scores.
- 48/60 runs under‑perform this bound; 31/60 are worse than a small‑model distillation baseline with equal token budget.
- Nevertheless, bottling can achieve large savings: Opus 5 retains ~82% of its zero‑shot macro‑F1 on query‑product relevance while cutting reported cost ≈657×.
- Compared to Jev, a purpose‑built “system‑one” model, Opus 5 recovers ~94% of Jev’s macro‑F1 at only 25% of Jev’s projected full‑work cost.

Implication: Bottling shows promise for cost‑effective large‑scale inference, but current LLM agents exhibit inconsistent ability to translate zero‑shot strength into economical, task‑specific solutions.
signals.brief_ar:
العنوان: وكيل في زجاجة – هل يمكن لوكلاء نماذج اللغة الكبيرة تحويل قدراتهم العامة إلى حلول رخيصة وقابلة للتوسع؟

تتفوق نماذج اللغة الكبيرة في مهام ضيقة متعددة، لكن تشغيلها لملايين المرات يكلف كثيرًا. مفهوم "التعبئة" يطرح سؤالًا: هل يستطيع وكيل LLM أن يخلق حلًا مخصصًا للمهمة يوازن بين جودة الإجابة وتكلفة الاستخدام المتراكمة؟ معيار BOTTLED يزوّد الوكلاء بعبء عمل غير مُعلَّم مع حدود ثابتة للوقت، الحوسبة، واستخدام واجهة برمجة التطبيقات؛ ويمكن للوكيل اختيار التدريب على نموذج صغير، كتابة برنامج قابل لإعادة الاستخدام، أو أي نهج آخر.

النتائج الرئيسية (10 نماذج، 3 مهام):
- الأداء القوي في الصفر‑شوت لا يضمن نجاح التعبئة؛ العديد من التجارب تقع تحت الحد الأدنى لثقة 95٪ لأدائها الصفر‑شوت.
- 48 من أصل 60 تجربة دون المستوى؛ 31 تجربة أقل من خط أساس التقطير بنموذج صغير بميزانية توكنات مماثلة.
- رغم ذلك، يمكن للتعبئة تحقيق وفورات كبيرة: نموذج Opus 5 يحتفظ بـ≈82٪ من ماكرو‑F1 الصفر‑شوت لتصنيف صلة الاستعلام بالمنتج مع خفض التكلفة ≈657 مرة.
- مقارنةً بـ Jev، نموذج "النظام‑الأول" المصمم لتكلفة منخفضة، يحقق Opus 5 حوالي 94٪ من ماكرو‑F1 لـ Jev مقابل 25٪ فقط من تكلفة Jev المتوقعة.

الاستنتاج: تظهر التعبئة إمكانات لتقليل تكلفة الاستدلال على نطاق واسع، لكن الوكلاء الحاليين غير ثابتين في تحويل القوة الصفر‑شوت إلى حلول اقتصادية مخصصة.

Title: Aditya31398/agentdynamics

Brief: This open‑source project provides an Application Performance Monitoring (APM) framework for AI agents. It generates flow maps and performs workflow process mining to visualize agent interactions. The suite includes cost and reliability metrics, and a process‑review component that integrates with LangGraph, OpenTelemetry, and the Anthropic/OpenAI SDKs as well as Claude Code. signals.title: Sherpa: Teaching LLMs to Teach Adaptively
signals.content: Large language models (LLMs) have become increasingly capable problem solvers, but being able to solve a problem is not the same as being able to teach it. Existing approaches to training LLMs as teachers rely on demonstrations, preference data, or predefined pedagogical criteria that specify what good teaching looks like. However, these signals are often not grounded in individual student learning outcomes, where effective teaching strategies can vary substantially across learners. To address this, we introduce Sherpa, a multi-turn reinforcement learning framework that instantiates multiple student archetypes with LLMs conditioned on distinct learning preferences and trains a teacher model to adapt its instruction by directly maximizing their learning outcomes. Teacher LLMs trained with Sherpa improve instructed students' performance across all archetypes by an average of 20.5 percentage points. Under MathTutorBench's evaluation, Sherpa raises the overall pedagogy score from 52.5% to 79.2%, indicating better teaching responses. Our human studies show that the trained teacher is preferred over the base model in 79.6% of pairwise comparisons. Together, Sherpa trains LLM teachers to adapt to diverse simulated students and become better aligned with human teachers, paving the road towards AI tutors teaching real students.

signals.brief_en: Sherpa is a multi‑turn reinforcement‑learning framework that trains LLMs to act as adaptive teachers. By simulating diverse student archetypes with distinct learning preferences, the teacher model learns to maximise each student’s outcomes rather than following fixed pedagogical rules. In evaluations, Sherpa‑trained teachers raise student performance by an average of 20.5 percentage points, increase the MathTutorBench pedagogy score from 52.5 % to 79.2 %, and are preferred over the base model in 79.6 % of human pairwise comparisons. The approach demonstrates that LLMs can be conditioned to tailor instruction to individual learners, a step toward AI tutors that align more closely with human teaching practices.

The imagery shows increased vehicle traffic, extensive debris removal, repairs to the damaged hillside and continuing earth-moving work in an area hit during the strike. Minzadayi has previously been linked to nuclear weapons-related research and development. The renewed activity may indicate efforts to restore capabilities damaged in March, although satellite imagery alone cannot confirm that nuclear weapons work has resumed. Source: Vantor Technologies
